# Weft 1.0.33
- Center worktree names and numbered badges inside sidebar selection highlights, in both active and inactive states. - Keep sample-preview labeling from changing the layout being checked.
Protected workspaces remain opt-in. Grok connections to protected workspaces remain blocked pending verification.

# Weft 1.0.32
- Keep the project sidebar visible and remove its collapse button to avoid broken column dividers. - Rename a project from its sidebar menu. Names persist in Weft without changing repository folders, setup commands, or worktrees. - Replace tiny lock and warning markers with readable worktree status text, keeping checkout badges aligned. - Clearly label development previews as sample data.
Protected workspaces remain opt-in. Grok connections to protected workspaces and default activation remain blocked until verification passes.

# Weft 1.0.31
- Polish the project sidebar with consistent typography, aligned project artwork and numbered checkout badges that retain their green running state. - Bring the service column into the same visual style as the overview: compact rounded icon tiles, readable status subtitles, a running-service count and clearer Start/Stop controls. - Improve selected-row contrast while preserving native selection, arrow-key navigation, worktree actions and service context menus.
Protected workspaces remain an opt-in demo. Grok connections to protected workspaces and default activation remain blocked in code until independent verification passes.

# Weft 1.0.30
- Bring the Settings style into the workspace overview with grouped service rows, aligned utility actions and compact port information. - Complete the workspace status area with a colored state mark, running-service count, preview address, copy confirmation and Open preview / Stop actions together. - Align service restart controls and simplify their buttons. Starting and issue states keep their progress and recovery actions visible; status animation respects Reduce Motion.
Protected workspaces remain an optional demo. Grok connections to protected workspaces and default activation remain blocked in code until provider identity and alternate host-tool routes are independently verified safe.

# Weft 1.0.29
- Simplify Settings with aligned native controls, shorter descriptions and a smooth translucency slider without duplicate labels. - Match both workspace column dividers in thickness, color and full-height treatment, while preserving native resizing. - Add an optional protected web demo with automatic runtime setup, isolated execution and a read-only local preview. Nothing downloads or starts until you choose Connect demo.
Protected workspaces remain opt-in. Grok connections to protected workspaces and default activation are blocked in code until independent provider identity and host-tool bypass verification pass. The current demo checks do not establish that Grok cannot bypass isolation.

# Weft 1.0.28
- Verify Grok Bot’s Apple Developer ID publisher and running process before automatic setup. Send must belong to the exact focused composer’s own container. - Bound local connections, incoming traffic, per-credential concurrency, long waits and per-agent report storage. Slow clients run outside Swift’s cooperative executor. - Add operator credential expiration and app-owned renewal, with a persisted migration deadline. Rotate the broader CLI token on API startup and during daily maintenance. - Enforce socket read deadlines using polling. Fix the macOS CLI response-read regression in withdrawn build 36, including delayed responses arriving in multiple chunks. - Preserve the live socket when another Weft instance fails to start, and reject oversized final request frames.
External bots with unrestricted access to the same macOS account still share filesystem permissions. These changes do not provide OS-level isolation between those bots.

# Weft 1.0.26
- Connect Grok Bot agents without copying and pasting setup instructions. After one-time macOS Accessibility permission, Weft opens the selected bot and sends its connection setup automatically. - Existing drafts stay intact. Setup delivery has its own retry, separate from creating or preparing a worktree. - Durable handoff history prevents duplicate sends after reconnects or interrupted delivery. Account and workspace ownership are checked again before submission.
Requires Grok Bot 0.75.3 or later. Enable Weft in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility when prompted. “Setup sent” confirms submission, not completion of the bot's setup task. Existing Grok Bot tool permissions still apply.

# Weft 1.0.25
- Connect an agent before it has a worktree. Choose its project and let Weft create and prepare a dedicated worktree, assign ports, and enable local tool and operator access. - Reuse an existing agent assignment or explicitly link an existing checkout. Keep its branch, files, and valid operator credential. - Resume connection after project configuration or changed-recipe review. Failed setup stays visible and does not claim a completed connection. - Show the workspace path, branch, and preview after connection, with instructions to hand off to the agent app. CLI operator credentials are discovered automatically from its assigned worktree. - Grok Bot setup and existing worktree links now include operator access. Grok Bot’s roster integration remains read-only; paste its handoff once into the bot conversation.

# Weft 1.0.24
- A simple, resizable Operator window using native grouped settings: agent switches, reports, and recent activity on one page. - Every registered agent is visible, with its linked worktree and operator access status. Enable all linked agents in one action without resetting existing connections. - Agents can use operator commands directly from their own worktree; private scoped credentials are discovered automatically. - Open reports to review evidence and reply. Earlier notices and technical details stay tucked away until needed. - Reduce background CPU use by pruning unrelated service directories during restart checks, reusing log timestamp formatting, and refreshing operator lifecycle data only when events change.

# Weft 1.0.23
- Add Operator Inbox: one consolidated view of worktree reports, recommended next steps, replies, approval-waiting items, and lifecycle notices. This first version collects evidence and communicates status; it does not execute repairs. - Enable scoped operator credentials for registered agents linked to worktrees. Rotate or revoke access from the inbox. Reports and notices remain restricted to the linked agent and worktree. - Add operator report, status, wait, and acknowledge commands to the CLI and MCP bridge, with durable issues, deduplication, redacted log excerpts, bounded notice pages, and resumable waits. - Deliver restart/relaunch reasons, memory warnings, failure, recovery, and stop notices to enabled worktree inboxes. Keep existing service policies unchanged. - Recognize already-running servers earlier after launch. Show detected services in the sidebar, service list, detail pane, and CLI without claiming ownership or reporting unchecked health checks as passing.
Requires macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon. Enable CLI and agent access in Settings, then open Operator Inbox → Agent access to connect a linked agent.

# Weft 1.0.22
- Fix dependency setup failures in Vite Plus projects using hostname routing. Preserve Vite's filesystem paths so its bundled CLI can be found while keeping shared hot reload working. - Keep long setup errors within a compact sheet with expandable, scrollable details and a Copy Details button. - Name the affected worktree in setup and operation errors, even when another checkout is selected.
Requires macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

# Weft 1.0.21
- Adjust window translucency with a live, saved slider in Settings → Appearance, or turn it off. Keep the project sidebar lighter and the service and detail columns matched across the full range. - Respect macOS Reduce Transparency by using opaque surfaces and disabling the translucency slider while that accessibility preference is enabled. - Click a worktree's warning icon to see why it needs attention and open Requirements, review settings, link an agent, or review a repair as appropriate. Keep warning actions accessible to keyboard and VoiceOver users.
Requires macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

# Weft 1.0.20
- Open worktrees through optional project-configured hostname routing, with readable agent names, consistent Open links and CLI status, streaming and WebSocket support, and direct-port fallback. - Connect approved agents from a shared Grok Bot roster to standing worktrees. Keep existing folders and ports when linking or renaming an agent. - Avoid unnecessary dev-server restarts during commits. Configure restart triggers, pause automatic restarts, restart manually, and see the reason in service logs. - Assign service ports consistently, including commands launched through package scripts. Explain occupied ports and keep optional service failures from stopping healthy required services. - Report crashed services accurately, retry preparation with a fresh operation, expose setup errors and logs in the CLI, and track existing remote branches automatically. - Improve checkout status, navigation spacing, active tabs and running-worktree indicators while keeping service ports visible.
Requires macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon. Hostname routing and agent connections are opt-in. Existing projects keep their current behavior until configured.

# Weft 1.0.19
- Install the pnpm version declared in mise.toml instead of repeatedly installing an incompatible version. - Automatically check Heimdall and Brand Boost credentials against AWS before Pi starts. Refresh stale keys after matching authentication failures and restart only Pi, with bounded retries and clear explanations when current keys remain rejected. - Apply credential recovery across Pattern Pi worktrees using each checkout's selected AWS account or its parent's account. Preserve local settings and keep private backups when keys change. - Show whether Company Sign-in is running on shared port 9090 and offer to start it from Requirements. - Display service ports in checkout and service details, and pass Storybook its assigned worktree port. - Preserve the underlying setup failure message so worktree repair explains what actually failed.

# Weft 1.0.18
- Add one standing Git worktree per actor, with stable port blocks, independent sessions, and a native sidebar for managed and external checkouts. - Add reviewed worktree setup, optional ignored-file copying, port templates, and environment identities for isolating local resources. - Keep shared services alive across consumers and protect their hosting checkout until they stop. - Add CLI and MCP worktree commands, persistent task claims, recoverable preparation, and in-app removal/prune approvals. Preserve parent checkouts, external processes, and Git branches.
- Give discovered existing worktrees the same service workspace and start, stop, and restart controls as Main, with automatic persistent ports. Keep selection passive, preserve existing files and branches, and skip creation hooks for existing folders. - Simplify navigation to checkout names and service status; move Git and port metadata into Checkout details and restore native sidebar and toolbar selection styling. - Discover agent-created worktrees through Git metadata listeners with a refresh fallback, show them automatically, and send actionable macOS notifications without a startup notification burst. - Add Delete Worktree… with current-state confirmation for existing and actor checkouts, preserving Main and Git branches. - Use compact single-line rows under every project, with quiet service indicators and native selection styling. - Show project favicons and aligned numbered checkout badges, with running colors and progress indicators for service operations. - Unify project, checkout, and service row heights; keep smaller service action symbols and move secondary actions into row context menus. - Group Start/Stop, Open, Restart, Build/Rebuild, and Logs in the service inspector, with technical details collapsed. - Show service status and running counts in Overview, and keep project preferences out of the primary action area. - Preserve the top-right toolbar button group while the startup indicator is displayed.
